Assistant to the Villain #3

Accomplice to the Villain

Hannah Nicole Maehrer

4.08
134,891 ratings17,132 reviews
Rate this book
Goodreads Choice Award
Nominee for Readers' Favorite Romantasy (2025)
REWARD OFFERED: Apprentice to The Villain wanted for treason (light), magical property damage (alleged), and one incident involving a weaponized scone (accurate). Frequently seen with a grumpy frog (crowned, judgmental). Answers to “Evie” or “Stop that.”

Evie Sage didn’t mean to become the right-hand woman to the kingdom’s most terrifying villain. One minute, she was applying for an entry-level position that promised “light paperwork and occasional beheadings,” and the next, she was knee-deep in magical mayhem, murder plots, and an entirely inappropriate crush on her brooding, sharp-jawed, walking disaster of a boss.

Now, with a magical prophecy unraveling, assassins showing up in the break room, and a suspicious amount of frogs wearing crowns, Evie has to figure out how to survive her job without setting the kingdom on fire―or her dignity, which is hanging by a very sarcastic thread.

Being evil-adjacent was never part of the five-year plan. But then again…neither was falling for The Villain.

October 11, 2025
Mini rant review

"You have been my downfall, Evie Sage, and now I... I will be your undoing."

Well, that turned out to be disappointing. I went in with high hopes given how much I enjoy this series but it's going downhill by the book (at least for me it is). There was so much that didn't work out for me and it pissed me off.

Starting with the plot, it's all over the place for me. No doubt that there's a direction for the storyline but the way it's executed is so messy. Like I get the author wants to create suspense and keep us on edge but to end every chapter on a cliffhanger like situation and then switching to a completely different pov that doesn't even connect to it just frustrated me. It doesn't need to happen every damn chapter!!

Speaking of multiple POVs, I hated it. I didn't care for the side characters. All I cared about was Evie and the Villain. But of course, the author wants to drag it out. The crumbs and little kisses is like a game that's going for too long and although I did get some satisfaction towards the end, it wasn't much.

The chemistry between the two is so good and the way the story is unfolding is not satisfying me. It's frustrating and dragging to the point that I only care about the two main characters getting together and the rest can just end up in a clusterfuck that it already is. The author just wouldn't let the romance bloom for the sake of angst and tension. Each and every moment between the two gets interrupted and it's annoying because it gives little room for growth and emotional intimacy. They're barely having conversations without anyone causing an issue.

I'll read the next book because it ended on a decently interesting note but I won't be having high expectations. The things I do for the Villain...

August 5, 2025
I have no words, this book was even better than I was expecting and I was expecting a lot!!
I was giggling and kicking my feet so much.. It gave me so much joy, but also pain.. It was so good!! Their banter is still unmatched, and so is the yearning!!

I fell in love with these characters the first time I met them, the very first tiktok Hannah posted. I've been here since the beginning and seeing them grow has been one of my favourite things ever.. Words will never be enough to describe how much I adore this world and its characters.

Their quest to fulfil the prophecy continues and it's as chaotic as ever. There's always mayhem when these characters are involved, but they never fail to make me laugh.
We discovered a lot and I personally loved that we got multiple POV's.

Trystan, I love him so much, my heart broke for him far too many times reading this.. I need to see him happy with Evie, causing chaos, more than anything.. I swear, if we don't get a novella or a long epilogue with them just being happy, I'm going to crash out.. He lost far too much, but seeing him slowly open himself to the feelings that were plaguing him was the pinnacle of this book.
Evie, she'll forever be one of my favorite characters ever, she brings a whole new meaning to the phrase kill them with kindness.. Seeing her drive The Villain crazy was the most fun I had in a while.. And she most definitely earned her promotion to accomplice and more. But her swallowing her feelings was truly heartbreaking, she deserves so much more.. And Trystan being the only one to see that did something to my heart!!

Tatianna and Clare are so adorable. I need them to be good..
And Kingsley, I love him so incredibly much, his chapters were my favourite.. Can't wait to see his story unfold..
I have to say, [redacted] really grew on me and him and Keeley are so fun to watch.. I need more of them.
And Bladen and Rebecka omg.. They are so darn cute!! And I loved her friendship with Evie and Tatianna in this book, it made me so happy..
Lyssa is, of course, a perfect little villain.
And to certain someones, I hope they take a long walk off a short pier.. or get pushed of a balcony..

It really was everything I wanted it to be and so much more.. There was so much anguish, as always, but this time I got so many moments I was craving since book one. * insert Kingsley holding his little sign "Finally" *
Yet, there was also moments that made me cry, one of them more than others, and betrayals I wasn't expecting.. I wasn't surprised at what happened near the end, I guessed it along the way and I have to say I'm delighted I was right. It's going to be so fun, now that everything is upside-down..

And that ending, excuse me.. How I'm to wait, I simply don't know how..
I need that next book!! I needed it yesterday tbh.. Seriously, how can I wait a year???

This book grabbed me by the throat and whispered “suffer beautifully.” And I did. 😮‍💨 RTC!

ೃ ⁀➷ Pre-view:🎯

🗡️ Back in the kingdom of Reneddawn—Where the Hickory Forest looms, danger brews in every shadow,villains reign, hearts are broken, and tea is always poisoned.

In the dangerously delightful third installment of fantasy romcom-Assistant to the Villain series...

Evie’s back—battle-scarred, banter-ready, and villain-approved.
She’s no longer just the assistant. She’s the partner-in-crime, emotional support human, and the villain’s possible downfall. Oops.

🪄➴ WHAT TO EXPECT (and possibly get cursed over):

📌The Villain Trystan— emotionally constipated, devastatingly sharp-jawed, morally questionable. Also: cape game? Unmatched.
📌 – A sunshine assistant with questionable morals (Evie, it’s you)
📌 – A brooding boss who cannot emotionally regulate
📌 – One magical prophecy with a flair for drama
📌 – Breakroom assassins. Like, literally.
📌“You're not supposed to care” / “Then stop looking at me like that” vibes- ANGRY LOVE CONFESSIONS!! I am expecting this!
📌-Grumpy x sunshine. Villain x chaos gremlin. Sarcasm x slow-burn desire.
📌-Workplace tension so intense it should be outlawed under kingdom law.
📌 –Because when your HR policy includes murder and your love language is vengeance, you know it’s about to get wild.
📌-And yes—Kingsley the frog still wears his crown, judges everyone, and may or may not run the entire kingdom from a teacup.
📌-There’s betrayal, banter, and one very awkward attempt at feelings. Chaos reigns. The assistant is in charge. The kingdom better buckle up.
📌 - Emotional trauma served with a side of scone violence
📌 – The fate of the kingdom maybe?? Who knows.
📌 – A dagger, a crown, and a suspicious amount of enchanted HR forms
📌 – I could fix him. Or I could help him burn everything.
📌- The Villain being emotionally unavailable in 4K
📌 – That frogs. Watching. Judging!
📌 – Romance, betrayal, destiny, and deeply inappropriate banter

Who needs therapy when you can assist, apprentice, or become an accomplice to the villain Right!?😏

The kingdom’s cracking.
The villain’s unraveling.
And Evie? She’s not just surviving this story anymore.
She’s writing it.

🥂 Let the chaos reign.
And may the most chaotic heart win.

Here I go!!🤸🏻‍♀️

"Sage, what the fuck are you doing?"

Perfect quote. No notes.

Seriously though, I feel like such a grump for saying this but I am so freaking over the qUiRkY humor.

I admit, I did kind of enjoy it in book 1 - sometimes the humor was a bit much but I liked the one-off silliness...that has absolutely lost its charm by the third book and I half want to strangle all of the characters.

Everyone has a quip, zingy one-liner, or biting remark and they always have to tack those on to every conversation. All of their personalities are starting to blend because they all have the same humor.

So much of Sage's behavior leans towards the "RAWR i'M sO rAnDoM" of the early 2000s that it is driving me nuts - and there's never any consequences for her boneheaded behavior.

There aren't any stakes to this book because I know the author will always write a way out for everyone (seriously, how many times has died and come back again? I lost count.

Everything in the plot just feels so convenient. Characters are dead until the plot needs them alive, obscure curses/magic can be reversed when suddenly the main characters discover a secret way to do it...just...stop.

After slogging through two books and just barely keeping my head above water for the third...I don't know if I will have the energy for a fourth (and hopefully final) book.

── ⋆˙⟡ 3.75 stars! ★
﹒⌗﹒ contains spoilers﹒౨ৎ˚₊‧

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ “i’m not doing this because of what they’d do. i’m doing it because it’s what i do.”

﹒ ⋆ ꩜ ⋆ 𓂃 ₊ ⊹

⟢ ⌗ ⋮ my thoughts♟️ ིܳ ﹾ ⸝⸝
ৎ this was fun… but like. did we really need this book?? i loved books 1 and 2. read them back to back. had a blast. but this one? i don’t know. i still had a good time, especially in the first half. i was laughing, i was enjoying myself, everything felt chaotic in a fun way. and then halfway through i just started losing interest. it wasn’t even bad, i just… stopped caring as much. the pov switches weren’t helping either. everything felt scattered and slow. i know plot stuff happened but it didn’t feel like it. like there’s a prophecy and death magic and traitors and shit falling apart—but it still somehow felt like no one was doing anything. they were just messing around.

and okay maybe that’s partially on me for not rereading, but i was so confused sometimes. like are we seriously doing the traitor thing again?? didn’t we already go through this exact plotline in books 1 and 2?? and now in book 3 we find out who it is… kinda… and they’re just still hanging around?? and no one figured it out last book?? i don’t know, i’m kinda tired of the whole traitor mystery thing at this point. i need them to start using their brains.

i do still love the tone of this series. even when things get dark it still feels lighthearted and fun. but fun doesn’t fix bad pacing. or weird plotting. i think i just expected more from this one and didn’t really get it.

﹒ ⋆ ꩜ ⋆ 𓂃 ₊ ⊹

⟢ ⌗ ⋮ characters♟️ ིܳ ﹾ ⸝⸝
ৎ evie has never been my usual type of fmc, but i do like her in this series. she’s such a chaotic little menace and i love how this book really leaned into her villain arc. she’s become way more comfortable with violence, and i’m obsessed with how her brain just has no filter anymore. she does get annoying sometimes, especially when she’s clearly pushing just to get a reaction (bathtub scene… you know what you did), but it’s never enough to make me actually dislike her.

ৎ trystan finally got over himself and stopped spiraling over the prophecy which. good. proud of him for putting his brain cells to use. i still really like him but he was a little much last book and i’m glad he’s slightly less emo now. i like how ride or die he is for evie even when he’s trying to stay away from her. he’s just a little pathetic about her and it’s fun.

ৎ side characters were mostly fun. becky, blade, tatianna, clare—love them. kingsley continues to be one of my favorites (even if that ending made me go huh???). gideon’s fine. keeley exists. nura was just there to take up space. lyssa didn’t irritate me this time, so that’s a win. i still don’t really care about some of them though, and the pov jumping made it worse. not all of them needed page time.

﹒ ⋆ ꩜ ⋆ 𓂃 ₊ ⊹

⟢ ⌗ ⋮ romance♟️ ིܳ ﹾ ⸝⸝
ৎ they finally got together! yay! but also… i didn’t really feel much? like yeah, they kissed, said i love you, had some sweet moments. but none of it made me feel excited. maybe it’s just me, but i wanted something that actually felt like a big deal now that they’re actually a couple.

﹒ ⋆ ꩜ ⋆ 𓂃 ₊ ⊹

⟢ ⌗ ⋮ extras♟️ ིܳ ﹾ ⸝⸝
— evie’s descent into villainy is still the best part of this series. love her unhinged era.
— the humor works. i laughed. no notes.
— the pacing was bad. there’s no other way to put it.
— can we retire the traitor twist. forever.
— objectively? a lot went down. subjectively? meh.
— i genuinely don’t know how to talk about this book. i remember vibes, not plot.

﹒ ⋆ ꩜ ⋆ 𓂃 ₊ ⊹

⟢ ⌗ ⋮ overall♟️ ིܳ ﹾ ⸝⸝
ৎ still a fun time. i enjoyed it enough. but compared to books 1 and 2, this is definitely the weakest one for me. the pacing was off, the plot didn’t move enough, and the second half lost me. there were fun moments and really great banter and chaos like usual, but i was expecting more. more development, more payoff, more reason for this book to exist. i’m not mad i read it, and the ending did leave me a little excited to see where things go, but this one just didn’t do much for me.

𐙚⋆˚✿˖° Okay… so Accomplice to the Villain absolutely wrecked me in the best way possible 😭.

⭐️ 4.5 stars (and trust me, it would’ve been a full 5 if not for that plot twist at the end 👀).

──★ ˙🧷 ̟ !!

First of all, listening to this in audio was a whole other experience. Em Eldridge’s narration? Perfect. Evie’s unhinged one-liners had me cackling in public 💀 and Trystan’s voice?? Yeah… let’s just say the slow burn finally decided to stop crawling and my ears were BLESSED 🤭. After three books of waiting, the payoff was everything.

Characters stealing the spotlight:

- Evie — my chaotic sunshine disaster queen 💖. Neurodivergent-coded, accidentally stabbing people, and still finding ways to turn weaponized scones into a power move. Iconic.

- Trystan — THIS MAN. Dark, broody, yearning out loud… his “I did not have a choice in loving her” speech? I screamed. Out loud. Marry me, sir.

- Kingsley — my shady little frog prince 🐸. Sir, you’ve been writing sneaky notes this whole time?? King behavior.

- Tatiana & Clare — the girlies deserve happiness pls, protect them at all costs.

- Amara — …fall into a ditch.

There were so many tiny moments I adored—Evie blurting her feelings 50 times before Trystan finally cracked, Kingsley holding up his sarcastic little signs, Becky + Evie’s friendship turning into pure gold. Those softer, chaotic beats are why this series feels so cozy despite all the blood, betrayals, and prophecies 😭.

─── ౨ৎ˚⟡˖ ࣪

BUT HANNAH. WHY that cliffhanger??? I was convinced this was a trilogy. Now suddenly it’s not? Please don’t milk it and ruin the quality—I love this series too much to see it dragged out. That said… yes, I will be rotting on the floor until book 4 drops 💋.

This book was messy, hilarious, romantic, and way more intense than the others, but still gave me that fairytale-satire sparkle ✨. If you love banter, found family chaos, and slow-burn grumpy/sunshine pining so strong it could fuel a kingdom, this series is for you.

𓇼🌊⋆★ Hannah Maehrer is officially the queen of cliffhangers, and I’m both obsessed and suffering.

Like, I thought this was gonna be a total letdown compared to the spark that the last two books made me feel. BUT THEN. OH. MY. GOD. After that 50% mark??? It SNAPPED. It GAVE. It FED ME EVERYTHING I WANTED AND MORE. I AM OBSESSED. I CAN’T BREATHE .I AM IN LOVE. THEY ARE MY WHOLE ENTIRE HEART AND MUST BE PROTECTED AT ALL COSTS. Seriously, my babies are SO PRECIOUS. The romance???I felt there love . IN. MY. BONES. IN. MY. SOUL . I was tearing up out of sheer awe because HOW ARE THEY THIS PERFECT??? eg:The ship scene in chapter 67(honestly owns my whole heart btw)—wasn’t sad in the slightest, but it was so incredibly precious and wholesome. It made me feel everything all at once; I was completely swept away in the moment. I actually had tears streaming down my cheeks, just because it was that beautiful and full of heart. And all those angry love confessions had me screaming the house down!!!

𝙏𝙍𝙔𝙎𝙏𝘼𝙉 𝙈𝘼𝙍𝙑𝘼𝙄𝙉 UGHHH THIS MANNN 🤸🏻‍♀️🧎🏻‍♀️🤸🏻‍♀️ he was sooo patheticly down bad for Evie in this book—the way he takes note of everything she does, is always there for her and can tell when her smile is fake. MAN literally made his enemies in mid battle sing happy birthday day to Evie *swoon* 😭🥺And Y'all HE DIDN'T HAVE A CHOICE WHEN IT CAME TO LOVING HER!!
As for 𝙀𝙫𝙞𝙚—do not underestimate her just because she is bubbly, forgiving, loving to the core and a bundle of sunshine that also will give you the worst second hand embarrassment at times—but beneath all that lies a deadly boss bish with an extremely cunning mind !!! She will litteraly smash your brains out if you say something bad about m̶y̶ her Trystan. Legit one of my fav fmc's ever!!

(🌀)𝓖𝓲𝓭𝓮𝓸𝓷+𝓚𝓮𝓮𝓵𝓮𝔂:I just need to talk about them for a moment AHHH!! I swear I felt the tension between these two brewing since the previous book, but THIS one?? OMG, I am absolutely OBSESSED. The way I devoured every single crumb of them—peak enemies-to-lovers energy!!! Their banter? The tension? Simply delicious. And now I’m over here guilty for catching the fastest crush on Gideon because HELLO?? My man is smoother than butter, and the way he cares for Keeley… 🤭🤭 I honestly flew through the first 50% of the book mostly because of these two, hehehe. My one critique? I wish certain scenes had been fleshed out more, because at times moments felt a little rushed and abit messy!!

So this time, I’m focusing only on the new faces (or the ones I forgot to gush about before)!!

√KEELEY: omgg I love her smm!!! YOU CAN JUST FEEL THE FEMININE RAGE WITHIN HER VEINS— genuinely need her povs. Her dynamic with Gideon H-O-T . Best way to discribe her is Repunzel in parellal universe. It hurts so much to know about what she's been through, I littrely wanna give her the biggest hug.

√AMARA: I hate her with passion even more than the king!! the duo shot rot in the pits of hell!!! THAT SLAP WAS SO WELL DESERVED 👏👏👏

(🌊)The plot twist twisted—like, I knew there’d be one, but I wasn’t ready for this level of insanity. This literally changes everything, yet suddenly all the pieces click—the reason Trystan’s death magic was drawn to Evie finally makes sense. I was expecting something like fated mates or a curse, but wdym… EVIE IS THE OG VILLAIN?! And the fact that they share the same dark past, they didn't even know offf?! I can’t even begin to fathom the guilt crushing Evie both of the past and the death of Auther. And for one she didn't even have a choice —she was just a baby. THE FORESHADOWING THROUGHOUT THE SERIES IS HAUNTING ME, and Trystan — TRYSTANN IS THE PRINCE—the 'hero' in the prophecy IRONIC— THE SON OF THE KINGGGG  I can't process and wdym he has a true love who is not Evie —I refuse to accept that. I just know the next book is going to rip my heart into shreds.

Obviously Trystan and Evie switched roles but I have a strong feeling in my gut that there going to exchange dynamics and personality as well. OHH God the last chp flippin ruined meee —I was sobbing so bad😭😭 like just let my babies be together peacefully —DAMN YOU DESTINY!!! I neeeeeeeeeed the next book asap cuz the Cliffhanger has crushed my heart into bits!!!

Now, let’s talk about KINGSLEY—HE IS BACKKK AHHHHHHHHHHHHHH !!! HOW?? I NEED TO KNOW!!  I have a feeling that Winne has got something to do with it mark my words there endgame !! and is he not part of the prophecy anymore ? If he is then... how? cuz Trystan is the prince now. I'm a bit confused!!

HOW am I supposed to go back and reread the books after ALL THIS?! Like??? my heart is in SHAMBLES, and I will NEVER be normal about this series again!!! 😭📖💔

꒰🐸꒱ 𝓟𝓸𝓼𝓽-𝓡𝓮𝓪𝓭𝓲𝓷𝓰 𝓡𝓮𝓯𝓵𝓮𝓬𝓽𝓲𝓸𝓷𝓼:
Commencement Date: August 08, 2025 | Completion Date: August 14, 2025

3.5☆?

First time on Goodreads that one of my book reviews has hit 50 likes — thank you so much, y’all! 🥹 I’m literally crying right now. I want this review to scream phenomenal, but I’m struggling to make that happen because… I just can’t find the right words for this book.

As I said, it was good — but not quite up to my expectations. Then again, I’m not even sure how high those expectations were to begin with. At the start, I was really struggling to remember where we left off in the second book, and it frustrated me — that’s a big reason for my mixed feelings.

This one leaned heavily into romance, which I personally enjoyed less of. If you were on the verge of crying from the slow burn in the second book, you might love it. Personally, I would’ve liked to cry a little more. I wanted more urgency, more momentum from the prophecy and overarching plot — but I can’t deny the cliffhanger left me giddy for the next book.

I also LOVE Trystan’s fierceness toward Sage. He is so damn down for her — it’s obvious to everyone except him. Sage was bold too, and I liked that. The multiple POV system grew on me after initially irritating me.

The tone? Whimsical. Serious but funny. So much goofy energy. I just wish we had explored the main plot more instead of mostly using it as a backdrop for romance. Still, Hannah Maehrer is a mastermind at crafting romances that feel tailor-made for each character — every pairing feels inevitable.

⋆.˚✮quotes✮˚.⋆

Subordinate' implies I have some sort of control over you, Sage," he said quietly, tuming away to cinch the ties of his own apron at his back. And I would say, by all accounts, you're hardly below me."
"Even if he'd really like you to be." Blade grinned, appearing at Evie's shoulder. At her eye roll, he slung a muscular arm around her, his green sleeves billowing from his copper vest all the way to his wrists.
A metal spoon soared through the air and knocked Blade square between the eyes "Ow!" the dragon trainer yelped, releasing Evie as he rubbed at the spot with an accusatory look in his amber eyes
"Evie's mother is present, you disrespectful lout." The Villain took a threatening step toward the dragon trainer.
Blade rubbed his forehead, glaring. "I'm not the one undressing her
daughter with my eyes."

The Villain leaned down and spoke quietly in Evie's ear, his voice smoky and dark. "I don't need your books." His dark gaze on her was a caress, a finger running down her cheek. "I already have it." It felt like a secret confided and a bitter confession all rolled into one.
What in the deadlands? "You already have what?"
His eyes lingered on her face, dipping to her red lips. "Inspiration." Now, why does that seemingly ordinary word suddenly sound absolutely
filthy?
Probably because he's saying it while staring at you like he wants to melt
your corset. And pathetically... it's working.

He had her. He always would.
Or was that just the concussion talking?
His dark magic swirled around them, flicking out the candles, shattering a stray ceramic chalice. "Sir, your magic?" she said sleepily as her boss carried her from the room. "Maybe someone else should take me to the healers
quarters."
"My magic doesn't matter." He was resolved in that. Evie could tell by how strongly he spoke the words, how the statement didn't seem at all emotional, just factual, pure logic in his mind. "No one touches you right now but me." She snuggled deeper into his chest, her heart beating for a different reason now as her arms clutched his neck. "I like possessive Evil Overlord. A new side to you," she said dreamily, drifting in and out of consciousness.
"Oh, Sage. If only you knew." There was too much subtext in the rough
words for her tired mind to pull apart.
Trystan had her. He had her.
But as Evie's eyes drifted shut, she sensed that this simple statement was
the gravest danger of all.

Gideon opened his mouth, and Sage speared him with a glare. "Do not suggest going to retrieve it, Gideon, or I will talk in detail about your awkward phase."
"Is he not still in it?" Keeley deadpanned.
Gideon glared at every person who laughed, so...everyone in the room.

"You don't scare me, Villain." He sneered, spitting in the direction Sage was standing in.
Trystan gripped the man's cheek with one hand, responding blandly,
"That's not a requirement for what's about to happen to you, but I caution you not to spit in her direction again unless you desire doing so without a tongue."

"I was staring at your chest," Evie blurted, her grin turning sheepish at te way his eyebrows shot to the top of his head.
"I beg your pardon?" he asked incredulously.
"I'm sorry?" Words continued rolling over her tongue, like a runaray carriage wheel. "You could stare at mine, too, if you want." What are you doing? she asked herself. Make it stop!
"To ensure we are, you know...even?"
WHAT ARE YOU DOING?
Amid her self-flagellation, her boss looked on the verge of a panic
attack.

He grabbed both her cheeks in his hands and crushed his lips back to hers.
He shut his eyes tight, the way he did when he was in pain. Trying to show her with everything he had that he loved her, too. The destiny monster may have decided their fate, but it couldn't have his mind, his thoughts, his kiss. And Trystan used all of them in that moment to show Evie he loved her more than life, more than breath... more than death. Kissing her more deeply, like he was defying the gods, defying destiny, defying everything that had ever told him he didn't deserve the precious thing he held in his hands.
He didn't need to deserve her. He was The Villain. He could take her, and
she could take him -

Evie put two fingers in her mouth and let out a whistle so loud she nearly shattered another window."I do understand that men derive enjoyment from interrupting women mid-sentence, so I'd hate to be a spoilsport, but could you all unkindly shut your traps so I may continue?"
Becky snapped her fingers in agreement without even looking up from
her notes.
Trystan's face went so red Evie began to worry.
"You may, uh, breathe, though," she said, and she swore she saw Trystan's chest begin to move again.
"So generous of you, little sister. Please continue, with our apologies." Gideon beamed with pride, which Evie shouldn't enjoy but of course did anyway.

"Why?" Amara laughed, and it was entirely without grace. "It's true, isn't it? You told me that last day that you would never feel anything for your family or anyone else ever again. I took you at your word. Or perhaps villains can't be held to such high standards? I should've known the moment I found out I was pregnant with you, you'd turn out exactly like—"
"I LOVE HER!"
The room went to a deadened silence at Trystan's hard proclamation. He didn't dare look anywhere but Amara, but he could feel Sage jerking at his side.
Amara's lips parted. "You love... who?"
"Her!" He gestured in a frustrated rage to Sage, without looking at her; he couldn't. The words couldn't travel back into his mind, though. They were out there in the open now. So he continued. "Everything I vowed when you betrayed me - that I'd never feel anything again -it was all useless against her. She weakened every defense you built. The moment i met her and every day since has been irritating, confusing, stifling, frustrating, maddening, and absolute chaos. You cannot say I am incapable of caring for others. I've broken every promise I've made to myself I didn't have a choice" - his voice shook with rage and pain and longing - "in loving her."
Kingsley hopped on the table, holding up a single sign, little ball and chain
dragging behind him.
FINALLY.

‘He no longer had an assistant. He had an apprentice. A furious, maddeningly frustrating, and disgustingly beautiful apprentice.’ 🤣

…Prepare to be won over by Evie, the sunshine accomplice, and The Villain. Brace yourself for their brilliantly unique and quirky romance!

‘Evie Sage is meant to be your downfall, and you her undoing’

I have loved every minute of this series and the third instalment definitely did not disappoint…in fact: I HAVE NO WORDS - it was even better than I ever imagined 🥲😈🐸💖✨

The storyline follows their continued quest to fulfil the prophecy, and it is just as wacky and fun-filled as ever! Whether on-site at the mansion, or in the field, you can always expect mayhem when these characters are involved. I’m not going to say much more about the storyline as I don’t want to give ANYTHING away 🤐 but this book is laden with content!

It has been such a journey for these characters over the part few books but one thing is for sure: they have definitely not lost their charm! There is something so special about the way Hannah has written these stories. It isn’t just a magical tale. Words cannot describe the FEELING of entering into this world she has created.

The banter is incomparable. It is witty, and hilariously entertaining. Possibly even more so in this book than the previous two, as if that was possible! Furthermore, Evie has so much sass, it is pure perfection. She will forever be my favourite character in this book, but that isn’t to say there aren’t some other fantastic characters. Kingsley, for example. I love this frog so damn much! 🐸

In this book, Hannah treated us to many different POV. She executed it brilliantly, and I loved that it gave us a deeper insight into more of the characters. It definitely made me feel more connected to some of the newer characters in this series. However, I think Trystan’s (The Villain) POV was one of my favourites to read. He is such an original character. Really, there is nobody else like him. His quirks and humour are second to none. I loved watching him be driven crazy by Evie 🤭 but, I felt for him so much at the same time 🥺

‘Every missing piece of her felt like it had come home.’ 🥰

Overall, this was an incredible read. The storyline, characters and tone of the book were all perfect. I officially have NO complaints. It was much more content heavy than I expected and, although there were moments I had been longing for, there were also surprisingly betrayals. AND FINALLY, all I can say is: WHAT AN ENDING 😱😵‍💫👑😈💖🐸✨ Bring on book 4 (like RIGHT NOW) ‘nincompoops’ 🤣

5 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

“You have been my downfall, Evie Sage, and now I…I will be your undoing.” ❤️

I have mixed feelings about this book. The plot was very chaotic, at some points it was boring and then there was too much happening. Also the pacing was uneven, slow at times and too fast paced at other points. The writing was descriptive and easy to follow. I felt that the character development was lacking and the characters didn’t reflect on aspects of the story. Additionally, there were too many perspectives, I wished the book focused more on the Villain and Evie’s perspectives instead. I enjoyed the side characters especially Gideon, Kingsley, Clare, Becky and Tatianna, but I wanted to see more interactions from the Villain and Evie.

I loved how protective the Villain and Evie were of each other. I adored that the Villain only showed a soft side to Evie. The tension and angst between the Villain and Evie was amazing. I also could feel the connection between them and I loved the banter. I loved the romantic scenes between them. The development of their relationship was lacking and there wasn’t space for them to discuss their feelings for each other without being interrupted. There were times when both the Villain and Evie were inconsistent about their feelings and didn’t communicate about it enough. I enjoyed the ending, there were several surprises and it was exciting. Overall I enjoyed the tension and chemistry between the main characters but the plot was chaotic.
